headline: Claim Drew Lock (bid 7, drop Malik Willis) before Wed 12:05 AM PT — he's confirmed to start for Seattle with Darnold out this week; whether he's still starting by your week 6 bye is unresolved (reports range from a week 3 Darnold return to 4-6 weeks out).
summary: Danny's 1-0 lineup is otherwise set right for week 2: no starters carry an injury flag, so no auto-subs are needed. The one lineup fix left on the board is moving MarShawn Lloyd into FLEX over Tre Tucker — Lloyd is Green Bay's clear starter with Josh Jacobs out on the exempt list. A.J. Brown stays on IR; new reporting puts his ankle timeline at 6-plus weeks. Claim Drew Lock for this week's start regardless, but don't count on him solving the week 6 Burrow/Willis bye clash — Darnold's return timeline is too unsettled to call that fixed; revisit around week 4-5.

lineup.why: Lloyd is Green Bay's clear early-down back with Josh Jacobs on the exempt list into at least mid-November, projected for 10.7 carries plus 2.5 targets against Tucker's 5.3 targets in an offense built around Ashton Jeanty.
lineup.evidence: Packers GM Brian Gutekunst said Lloyd is 'as ready as he's ever been' with no injury designation in Sept 2-14 practice reports, and Jacobs' legal case (initial court appearance Nov 17) keeps him out well beyond this week; Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said the offense runs through Jeanty until Brock Bowers returns, capping Tucker's target share after a 4-target Week 1 (Sept 2026 reports).

adds.why: tier 2, bid 7 of your 145: a confirmed starter for this week with a bye (11) that differs from Willis's, priced low because reports disagree on how long Darnold is out, so Lock holding the job through your week 6 bye is a bonus, not a given.
adds.evidence: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said his early read is Lock starts Week 2 at Arizona with Darnold out (Sept 14-15 reports); Darnold's return timeline is unsettled — Rapoport reported he could be back as soon as week 3 (Sept 27), while Florio put it at 4-6 weeks, and the Seahawks call it short-term (Sept 15 reports) — so treat any week 6 coverage from Lock as provisional; Willis remains Miami's own QB1 but is Danny's bench QB3 with no path to starts here.

flags.what: IR, high-ankle sprain from Sept 9; reported Sept 10-13 to be out at least 6 weeks, likely into mid-October.
TB's 1B receiving-down back behind Bucky Irving, not a lead-back role (Sept 2026 reports).

Miami's own QB1, but Danny's bench QB3; recommended drop for Drew Lock this week.

watch.what: Return timeline is contested: Rapoport says possibly back week 3 (Sept 27), Florio says 4-6 weeks, Seahawks call it short-term. Track this before assuming Lock covers your week 6 bye.

alerts.title: ➕ Claim Drew Lock, drop Willis
alerts.body: Lock starts for Seattle with Darnold out; bid 7, drop Malik Willis, before the Wed 12:05 AM PT waiver run. Cheap depth and a bye that differs from Willis's, but Darnold's return timeline is contested (week 3 to 6 weeks out) — don't assume Lock is still starting by your week 6 bye.

alerts.title: 🔁 Start Lloyd over Tucker in FLEX
alerts.body: MarShawn Lloyd is Green Bay's clear starter with Jacobs on the exempt list; move him into FLEX over Tre Tucker before Sunday's 10 AM PT kickoffs.

alerts.title: 🔴 A.J. Brown out 6+ weeks
alerts.body: New reporting says Brown's high-ankle sprain keeps him out at least 6 weeks, into mid-October; he stays on IR, no action needed.
